title: Finite Q3 matching-layer common-core induced-norm envelope
question: Do the actual Z^3 matching bond layers and tensor-local onsite factors admit a two-sided K^(1/2) common-core envelope that is uniform in finite-box volume?

graph_model.colouring: axis plus parity of the lower endpoint coordinate
graph_model.matching_condition: each vertex is incident to at most one edge in each layer

hypotheses: K_f=sum_x f_x k_x with k_x >= 1+p_x^2/(2 chi)+gamma q_x^4
F is one matching layer and B_F(delta) shears p_u,p_v by +/-delta*c*q_v, +/-delta*c*q_u

onsite_factor.hypothesis: k_x is an affine shifted local h_x and all site-local self-adjoint terms strongly commute on the declared Schwartz/form core
onsite_factor.conclusion: A_t^* K_f A_t=K_f and endpoint graph norm is one

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks the scalar inequalities only; it does not encode unbounded operators, tensor domains, Trotter convergence, exhaustion, KMS or thermodynamic limits.

adversarial_review.check: The full Q3 box has degree six and is not one matching; the estimate is applied layer by layer.
The endpoint norm follows only under the declared positive self-adjoint K form and core hypotheses; the scripts do not prove those operator hypotheses.
Onsite norm one is conditional on affine local h_x and strong tensor commutation; it is not inferred from a finite matrix fixture.
The coefficient is volume-independent, but no boundary leakage or exhaustion summability is claimed.
A uniform graph envelope does not itself prove Lie-Trotter convergence or identify the limiting generator.
R208 checks scalar inequalities only and cannot certify the QFT operator theorem.
No heat_root_incidence or A1/R-192 production map is present.
